purpose: Viewport diagnostic: does a screenshot action viewport (1920x1080) resize the layout viewport persistently, and can the page then scroll? One page, one request.
notice: NOT SENT. Paid execution (diag-run) is a separate operator-gated command that HOLDS without --yes.
Provider cost is UNKNOWN beyond the documented 1 credit per scrape: screenshot/action/scan pricing is not published. The local ledger is a reservation allowance, not a provider cap.
Probes are read-only. The only page effect is window.scrollTo(0, 3000).
PNG size is the screenshot crop; compare it to innerHeight, root clientHeight, visualViewport and document height without assuming they are equal. Image differences alone do not prove scrolling.

actions.script: (function w2fDiagProbe() { const d = document.documentElement, b = document.body, vv = window.visualViewport, rect = (s) => { const e = document.querySelector(s); if (!e) return null; const r = e.getBoundingClientRect(); return { top: r.top, left: r.left, width: r.width, height: r.height, bottom: r.bottom, documentY: r.top + (window.scrollY || 0) }; }; return { w2f: "diag-probe", tag: "P0", innerWidth: window.innerWidth, innerHeight: window.innerHeight, rootClientWidth: d.clientWidth, rootClientHeight: d.clientHeight, visualViewport: vv ? { width: vv.width, height: vv.height, scale: vv.scale, offsetTop: vv.offsetTop, pageTop: vv.pageTop } : null, scrollY: window.scrollY, documentHeight: Math.max(d.scrollHeight, b ? b.scrollHeight : 0), devicePixelRatio: window.devicePixelRatio, readyState: document.readyState, features: rect("#features"), hero: rect("#hero") }; })();

(function w2fDiagScroll() { window.scrollTo(0, 3000); return { w2f: "diag-scroll", requested: 3000, scrollY: window.scrollY, innerHeight: window.innerHeight, documentHeight: Math.max(document.documentElement.scrollHeight, document.body ? document.body.scrollHeight : 0) }; })();
